issues.description: Header/implementation name mismatch for the sphere-intersection function: the header declares a function named check_sphere_hit(...) but the .cpp defines ray_sphere_intersect(...). main.cpp (the caller) uses ray_sphere_intersect(...). This inconsistent function declaration/definition prevents correct compilation or causes confusing linker errors for students because the prototype in the header does not match the implemented symbol or the usage in main.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declaration in ray_sphere_intersect.h match the actual function name and signature used and implemented. For example, replace the prototype 'bool check_sphere_hit(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius);' with 'bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius);' (or alternatively rename the implementation to check_sphere_hit). Ensure both template and solution repositories use the same prototype so students can compile and link without confusion.

issues.description: The sphere-intersection function is declared under a different identifier in the header than the name used in its implementation and at call sites. The header declares check_sphere_hit(...), but the implementation defines ray_sphere_intersect(...) and main.cpp calls ray_sphere_intersect(...). This mismatch breaks the straightforward mapping between API declaration, implementation, and usage and is likely to confuse students looking for where to implement or call the sphere intersection check.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function identifier consistent across declaration, implementation and call sites. For example, change the header declaration to: 'bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius);' or alternatively rename the implementation and all calls to 'check_sphere_hit' so the prototype, definition and usages use the same name.
